question_text:
What must you be prepared for when a truck in front of you wishes to turn right into a narrow street?
The truck will

options.text: - reduce speed drastically
- swing out to the left before turning
- move well over to the right

correct_answers.text: - reduce speed drastically
- swing out to the left before turning

comment: Keep a large distance from the lorry and under no circumstances overtake on the right-hand side, even if you would have the opportunity to do so as a two-wheeler driver. The road train must first reduce its speed considerably to turn. For reasons of space, the truck driver may then have to steer the towing vehicle far to the left so that the trailer or semi-trailer does not roll over the kerb when turning.

question_text: What do you have to particularly remember at crossroads and junctions in a built-up area?

options.text: Intersecting roads may have priority even though they are narrow and less well developed
A better developed road always has priority
The rule "right before left" applies without exception at all crossroads and junctions

correct_answers.text: Intersecting roads may have priority even though they are narrow and less well developed

comment: By driving on a wide and well-developed road, you don't automatically have the right of way. The rule "right before left" does not apply always and everywhere. Instead, signs or traffic lights regulate who has priority. Therefore, pay attention to the signposted right-of-way regulation or the traffic lights at each individual intersection and junction.

question_text: What must you be prepared for?

options.text: The appearance of a vehicle from the right
A longer braking distance on account of the wet, leaf-covered road
A vehicle coming from the right will give way despite having priority

correct_answers.text: The appearance of a vehicle from the right
A longer braking distance on account of the wet, leaf-covered road

comment: The wet leaves on the road significantly increase the braking distance of your vehicle. Adjust your speed accordingly. Also keep in mind that due to the non-existent priority traffic signs, the "Left yields to right" rule applies. You would have to give priority to a vehicle coming from the right, even if the driver is slow and hesitant to approach the intersection due to the weather.

question_text: Why must you be particularly careful here?

options.text: Because there is an increased danger of skidding when braking
Because a vehicle could come from the right
Because the car coming from the left has priority

correct_answers.text: Because there is an increased danger of skidding when braking
Because a vehicle could come from the right

comment: The wet leaves on the road result in a longer braking distance and a high risk of slipping. Therefore, reduce your speed and drive carefully before reaching the intersection. A vehicle could be coming from the right and you should give it the right of way. Since there are no signs at the intersection that give you the right of way, the rule here is "right before left".

question_text: You want to pull out of a row of parked vehicles into the stream of moving traffic. Behind you is a parked truck and trailer. How do you assess this situation?

options.text: Because of your restricted view, you cannot see approaching vehicles until they are very close
Because of their restricted view, vehicles approaching from behind cannot see your vehicle until very late
It is safe to pull out here because you are protected by the truck and trailer behind you

correct_answers.text: Because of your restricted view, you cannot see approaching vehicles until they are very close
Because of their restricted view, vehicles approaching from behind cannot see your vehicle until very late

comment: Because of the truck, you can hardly see the traffic behind you. It also obscures the view of the flowing traffic on your vehicle. You must therefore be particularly careful and slowly feel your way on the road. You may need to go back to avoid hazards.

question_text:
You are approaching a school. Children are leaving the school grounds. What must you reckon with?
That children

options.text: - rush onto the road without thinking
- ride their bicycles onto the road without paying attention
- always conduct themselves properly on the road

correct_answers.text: - rush onto the road without thinking
- ride their bicycles onto the road without paying attention

comment: In the vicinity of schools, you must always be prepared for children crossing the road abruptly. Children are not yet able to assess themselves and other road users very well and often react impulsively and in a way that is not appropriate for traffic. As a car driver, you must adapt your driving style accordingly in order to exclude any danger to children. In addition to driving at a low speed, you must be particularly attentive and ready to brake at all times.

question_text: What do hazard warning lights draw your attention to?

options.text: To vehicles which have broken down
To school buses with children boarding or alighting
To a traffic congestion

correct_answers.text: To vehicles which have broken down
To school buses with children boarding or alighting
To a traffic congestion

comment: The use of the hazard warning lights is subject to strict rules. You may only switch on the hazard warning lights to secure your broken-down vehicle or to indicate a traffic jam or a school bus. A school bus with its hazard warning lights on may only be overtaken at walking speed.

question_text:
A big combine harvester in front of you wishes to turn right. What is correct?
The combine harvester

options.text: - will swing far out to the left when turning
- will slow down drastically before turning
- cannot swing out due to rear-wheel steering

correct_answers.text: - will swing far out to the left when turning
- will slow down drastically before turning

comment: The combine harvester needs to gain amplitude to turn because the turn is very narrow. To do this, it will greatly reduce his speed. Keep your distance and also drive slowly and be prepared to brake. Especially for cyclists: Never overtake on the right!

question_text: You are driving behind a farm vehicle with a trailer carrying a high load. What must you reckon with?

options.text: Particularly when braking or turning, parts of the load can fall off
The indicators may be concealed, making it difficult to see when the combination of vehicles wishes to turn off
The braking distance of the combination of vehicles is particularly short because of its load

correct_answers.text: Particularly when braking or turning, parts of the load can fall off
The indicators may be concealed, making it difficult to see when the combination of vehicles wishes to turn off

comment: If you are riding behind an agricultural vehicle with a heavily loaded trailer, you must expect the following: Part of the load could fall onto the roadway when turning or braking. The indicator could be dirty or covered by the load. The braking distance of the vehicle is increased by the weight of the load.

question_text: What should you anticipate?

options.text: Pedestrians crossing the road
A vehicle driving past the bus
That I will have to stop at the junction

correct_answers.text: Pedestrians crossing the road
A vehicle driving past the bus
That I will have to stop at the junction

comment: You must expect to have to stop before the intersection when turning. For one thing, the view of the bus coming from the right is obstructed. In addition, other vehicles could pass it. In addition, pedestrians may also want to cross the road. You must always show special consideration for them.

question_text: What should you do in this situation?

options.text: Reduce speed
Be ready to brake
Continue driving as before

correct_answers.text: Reduce speed
Be ready to brake

comment: The driver of the vehicle coming out of the exit cannot see the cross traffic. He would have to be directed into the traffic. He could drive further ahead and prevent you from continuing your journey. You should reduce your speed, be ready to brake, even stop if necessary.

question_text:
Why do you have to wait before turning right?
Because of

options.text: - the pedestrian
- the cyclist
- the van

correct_answers.text: - the pedestrian
- the cyclist

comment: If you want to turn right, you will need to let all the vehicles drive past that meet you. This also applies to bicycles that go into the same direction as you. Likewise, you must give priority to pedestrians who want to cross the road in front of you.

question_text:
What should you anticipate in this situation?
The oncoming car will now

options.text: - pull out and cross the centre of the road
- brake and not cross the centre of the road
- overtake without crossing the centre of the road

correct_answers.text: - pull out and cross the centre of the road

comment: Because the oncoming vehicle is being slowed down by a bicycle, you should expect the vehicle to overtake the bicycle. If this happens, the vehicle could cross into your lane. In the event that the driver does not brake, you should keep as far to the right on the road as possible. Also, be prepared to brake so that you can react to any situation as quickly as possible.

question_text: You want to turn right at the junction. What is the right thing to do?

options.text: I change lanes as early as possible
I may not impede cyclists in the cycle lane
I may only cross over the cycle lane at walking speed

correct_answers.text: I change lanes as early as possible
I may not impede cyclists in the cycle lane

comment:
There is a protective lane for cyclists between your lane and the turning lane. It is part of the carriageway and is separated by a broken line.
You may only use the protective lane to change lanes, swerve or turn. If you use it, you are not allowed to obstruct cyclists or come to a standstill in the protective lane. You should therefore change lanes as early as possible.

question_text: When could a dangerous situation arise here?

options.text: If I continue driving at the same speed
If [the cyclist] changes to my lane
If [the cyclist] stops at the end of the cycle path

correct_answers.text: If I continue driving at the same speed
If [the cyclist] changes to my lane

comment: You can see that the cycle path ends immediately in front of you. The cyclist would have to stop and wait until she can safely merge into the flowing traffic. However, rather than stopping, expect her to swing into the lane in front of you.

question_text: What must you watch out for when turning right here?

options.text: For the cyclist
For oncoming traffic
For the motorbike

correct_answers.text: For the cyclist

comment: Before you can turn right, you have to let the cyclist on the bike path to your right pass by. Cyclists have priority when they drive in your direction. Cyclists in oncoming traffic have no priority. Nevertheless, watch out for them to avoid danger.

question_text: What should you do?

options.text: I stop
I drive carefully past to the right of the truck
I move into the middle lane now

correct_answers.text: I stop

comment: Since there is a car in the blind spot to the left of you and on the other side a truck wants to turn right into the construction site, you should stop. Do not drive on the middle lane. Wait for the truck to clear the road. Then you can continue.

question_text:
What should you note about electric bicycles (e-bikes) participating in road traffic?
E-bikes can

options.text: - be deceptively fast
- look very similar to conventional bicycles
- be easily recognised due to their engine noise

correct_answers.text: - be deceptively fast
- look very similar to conventional bicycles

comment: E-bikes are just as quiet as classic bikes and are therefore often perceived late. However, they often achieve significantly higher speeds than bicycles without an engine. This is underestimated by many road users, so dangerous situations can occur surprisingly. In general, expect cyclists to gain speed and perform speedy maneuvers.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I get ready to brake
I watch [the cyclist] closely
I manoeuvre over to the left side of the road

correct_answers.text: I get ready to brake
I watch [the cyclist] closely

comment: You should be ready to brake and watch the cyclist carefully, because the cyclist can suddenly ride onto the road.

question_text: You wish to overtake a farm tractor with a mounted implement extending beyond its back. What must you remember?

options.text: The mounted implement can swing out when the tractor turns off
The rear lights may be heavily soiled or concealed, making direction signals difficult or impossible to see when they are on
Farm tractors can always be overtaken safely due to their low speed

correct_answers.text: The mounted implement can swing out when the tractor turns off
The rear lights may be heavily soiled or concealed, making direction signals difficult or impossible to see when they are on

comment: You should always refrain from an overtaking maneuver when the tractor wants to turn. The reason for this is that the tractor has a large turning circle and is likely to veer, blocking the road. Also keep in mind that the turn signals of such a vehicle are not always visible and that they could be covered by dirt due to the agricultural use.

question_text: What must you anticipate on the other side of this crest in the road?

options.text: A vehicle may be stationary there
There may be an oncoming vehicle on my side of the road
There may be a slow moving vehicle on my side of the road

correct_answers.text: A vehicle may be stationary there
There may be an oncoming vehicle on my side of the road
There may be a slow moving vehicle on my side of the road

comment: Due to the height of the crest, it is not possible to see what is behind it. Expect to encounter obstacles there, such as broken-down or slow-moving motor vehicles. Also be prepared for oncoming trucks sharing your lane. To be able to react to such dangers in time, you should reduce your speed accordingly.

question_text: What do you do?

options.text: Brake and move to the right
Proceed without taking action so that the truck is forced to pull back over to the right

correct_answers.text: Brake and move to the right

comment: When a truck overtakes a cyclist crossing the continuous line, you must never try to push the truck back onto its lane. Brake instead and go far enough to the right.

question_text: What must you be prepared for in this situation?

options.text: An uneven and dirty roadway
Workers and construction equipment on the roadway
Police regulating traffic

correct_answers.text: An uneven and dirty roadway
Workers and construction equipment on the roadway

comment: In the area of ​​a construction site you have to drive carefully and reduce the speed. For one, the road can be dirty. But it there can also be workers, construction equipment or construction vehicles on the road and obstruct the traffic.

question_text:
What must you be prepared for in this situation?
That the

options.text: - braking distance will be longer
- bus moves off immediately
- bus driver allows you to pass

correct_answers.text: - braking distance will be longer
- bus moves off immediately

comment: Due to the weather and the slush you have to expect a slippery road surface and a longer braking distance. The bus has priority over you and shows you by indicating that he wants to start driving. Carefully reduce the speed to allow it to veer. Under no circumstances may you overtake him.

question_text:
You are waiting at a traffic light and want to turn right. What should you remember?
You must

options.text: - make sure there is no road user beside you on the right intending to go straight on
- simply glance in the mirror to check that there is no cyclist behind you
- concentrate fully on the turning manoeuvre because any cyclist has to wait anyway

correct_answers.text: - make sure there is no road user beside you on the right intending to go straight on

comment: If other road users are next to you, you must give priority to them if you wish to drive straight ahead. So, also pay attention to people on bike and pedestrian paths. It is not enough to just keep track of the road through the rear-view mirror. In addition, you have to control your surroundings with a look back over your shoulder to be able to perceive those road users who are hidden in the blind spot of the mirror.

question_text: You are driving on a new road through a woodland area. What must you reckon with?

options.text: Wild animals unexpectedly crossing the roadway
An obstruction caused by an accident involving a wild animal
There is no reason to expect accidents involving wild animals on new roads

correct_answers.text: Wild animals unexpectedly crossing the roadway
An obstruction caused by an accident involving a wild animal

comment: When roads are newly constructed in forested areas, they often pass through the natural habitat of various wild animals. Therefore, it is possible that their habitual paths cross your roadway. For this reason, you must expect wildlife crossings and obstacles due to frequent wildlife accidents on forest roads.

question_text: Several deer run across the road in front of your vehicle. What must you reckon with?

options.text: There could be stragglers following the herd
The herd may come back and cross the road again
There is no reason to expect any more animals

correct_answers.text: There could be stragglers following the herd
The herd may come back and cross the road again

comment: If several deer flee across the road in front of your vehicle, you have to expect the following: several animals could follow. The entire herd could also turn in the opposite direction and switch to the other side of the roadway again.

question_text: At which time of the day do you have to reckon with increased wild animals crossing?

options.text: At dusk
At dawn
At noon

correct_answers.text: At dusk
At dawn

comment: Expect more deer crossings during the morning and evening twilight. This transitional period between day and night is characterized by diffuse light conditions.

question_text: Which dangers must you reckon with above all in rural areas?

options.text: Soiled roadways
Slow farm vehicles
Excessively wide farm vehicles

correct_answers.text: Soiled roadways
Slow farm vehicles
Excessively wide farm vehicles

comment: Where farming is practised, tractors and other agricultural vehicles travel at slow speeds and/or over width. Often the roadway is also dirty with soil or manure.

question_text: A farm tractor is approaching you at dawn with its headlights switched on. What must you reckon with?

options.text: The tractor can carry large work equipment which is difficult to see
Despite the headlights being switched on, it is not always possible to discern the width of the tractor
2 wide trailers can be attached to the tractor

correct_answers.text: The tractor can carry large work equipment which is difficult to see
Despite the headlights being switched on, it is not always possible to discern the width of the tractor
2 wide trailers can be attached to the tractor

comment: In agricultural vehicles, the lights are sometimes broken. They can also be covered up by dirt or tarpaulins. The width of the vehicles is not easy to assess. In addition, these vehicles can have up to two trailers.

question_text: What must you observe when you enter a tunnel?

options.text: Drive with dipped headlights also during the day even in well lit tunnels
Take off your sunglasses
Switch fog headlamps on

correct_answers.text: Drive with dipped headlights also during the day even in well lit tunnels
Take off your sunglasses

comment: Before entering a tunnel, you must note the following: there is a light obligation in a tunnel. Therefore, turn on the dipped beam to see and be seen better. If you have sunglasses, take them off. You must not switch on the fog lamp in the tunnel.

question_text: What must you do in case of a traffic jam in a tunnel?

options.text: Switch hazard warning lights on
When traffic comes to a standstill, keep a safety distance of approximately 5 m to the car ahead
Secure and leave vehicle immediately

correct_answers.text: Switch hazard warning lights on
When traffic comes to a standstill, keep a safety distance of approximately 5 m to the car ahead

comment: If there is a traffic jam in a tunnel, stop and turn off the engine. By keeping a safe distance of about five metres, you reduce the risk of poisoning, preserve a manoeuvring option and allow rescue vehicles to pass. Switch on the hazard warning lights to warn following drivers. Only leave your vehicle after an appropriate loudspeaker announcement.

question_text: What can impair your attention when driving through a tunnel?

options.text: Reflections of light from oncoming traffic
Length of the tunnel
Good road markings

correct_answers.text: Reflections of light from oncoming traffic
Length of the tunnel

comment: When passing through a tunnel, the following factors may interfere with your attention: the lack of visual stimulus and the monotony of speed, as well as the lights of oncoming traffic. In this case, an orientation on the right side of the road is helpful; avoid looking directly into the light of oncoming traffic.

question_text: What must you observe particularly when driving through a tunnel?

options.text: You may be distracted by very loud noise
Signs for safety installations such as emergency exits and emergency telephones
You may be distracted by light effects

correct_answers.text: You may be distracted by very loud noise
Signs for safety installations such as emergency exits and emergency telephones
You may be distracted by light effects

comment: Driving noises in a tunnel are considerably louder due to the reverberation of the tunnel walls. You can also hear the noise of the ventilation system. This has an irritating effect on you as a driver. Your eyes first have to get used to the different visibility conditions. The increased light reflections from oncoming traffic make things more difficult. The emergency signage is also distracting.

question_text: Which basic code of conduct must you observe in a tunnel?

options.text: Drive with dipped headlights also by day even in a well lit tunnel
Do not make a U-turn
Follow instructions and information from the tunnel personnel

correct_answers.text: Drive with dipped headlights also by day even in a well lit tunnel
Do not make a U-turn
Follow instructions and information from the tunnel personnel

comment: The following rules of conduct are mandatory in all tunnels: on the entire route no U-turns are allowed. Regardless of the lighting situation, the dim light must always be switched on. The instructions of the tunnel staff must always be followed. Personal protection antecedes the protection of vehicles and their security.

question_text:
Why are you required to stop here?
Because of

options.text: - the van
- the pedestrian
- the cyclist

correct_answers.text: - the van
- the pedestrian

comment: You want to turn left. A van approaching from the opposite lane also wants to turn into this road. The vehicle has priority. Likewise, you must pay attention to pedestrians who want to cross this street.

question_text: What should you do now?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to brake
Continue driving as before
Swerve to the left

correct_answers.text: Slow down and be ready to brake

comment: The white reversing lights of the vehicle that turned in front of you indicate that it would probably turn back to its original lane in reverse. Since you cannot tell if you have been noticed by the driver, you should reduce your driving speed and be ready to brake. Refrain from an evasive maneuver due to oncoming traffic.

question_text: You want to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Allow the cyclist to pass through the junction
Check way is clear by glancing over your shoulder
Take the turn ahead of the cyclist

correct_answers.text: Allow the cyclist to pass through the junction
Check way is clear by glancing over your shoulder

comment: Before you can turn, you have to check in the rear-view mirror if the road is clear. It is also advisable to look over your shoulder: this is the only way to be aware of dangerous situations located in the blind spot of the mirror. Keep in mind that other road users - cyclists or pedestrians - whose way you cross, always have priority.

question_text: What should you anticipate?

options.text: The motorbike could swerve to the left
The person beside the van could encroach further onto the road
Pedestrians could cross the road in front of the van

correct_answers.text: The motorbike could swerve to the left
The person beside the van could encroach further onto the road
Pedestrians could cross the road in front of the van

comment: The other road users can react to this situation with all the different scenarios described. All are equally dangerous. Therefore, extreme caution and slow driving is required.

question_text: Ahead of the motorbike a car is seeking to reverse on the road. What should you anticipate?

options.text: That the car continues to reverse
That the motorbike will suddenly brake
That my braking distance will be longer than normal

correct_answers.text: That the car continues to reverse
That the motorbike will suddenly brake
That my braking distance will be longer than normal

comment: Car drivers often underestimate the speed of approaching motorcyclists; the same happens to the driver here while he's pulling out of a parking space. The action alternatives of the motorcyclist - braking or dodging - are both dangerous for him on a snow-slicked road surface. He could fall. Also consider the longer braking distance in this weather.

question_text:
You are driving quickly along a main road and some distance ahead you see a deer close to the carriageway. What should you do?
I have to

options.text: - reduce speed
- be ready to brake
- perform an emergency braking manoeuvre

correct_answers.text: - reduce speed
- be ready to brake

comment: If the deer is not yet on the road, you should under no circumstances perform emergency braking. This would unnecessarily endanger other road users and force them to unpredictable reactions. Nevertheless, you should reduce the speed of your vehicle and keep it ready to brake: the animal could run without warning on the road.

question_text: Why are you particularly at risk, if you are riding a two-wheeler?

options.text: Because I can be easily overlooked
Because my speed can be underestimated
Because I am at greater risk of injury in the event of an accident

correct_answers.text: Because I can be easily overlooked
Because my speed can be underestimated
Because I am at greater risk of injury in the event of an accident

comment: Especially in restrictive visibility conditions such as fog and darkness, the small silhouette of the two-wheeled driver leads to the fact that he is recognized late or not at all. In addition, the small design makes it difficult to estimate its speed. In the event of a collision, two-wheelers generally offer less protection than most other motor vehicles.

question_text: Driving on a very busy road with several lanes, you have manoeuvred yourself into the lane for taking a left turn. Now instead of turning left, you want to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: I turn left
I reverse with my hazard lights turned on
Driving a wide curve, I turn right

correct_answers.text: I turn left

comment: A lane change or turning right could endanger other road users due to the heavy traffic. You must therefore turn left and take a small detour. Watch out for lane markings that prohibit you from changing lanes.

question_text: There is a tunnel on my route. What should I know?

options.text: I should know how I park and leave my vehicle if I am unable to continue driving
I should know how escape routes are indicated in tunnels
I can be sure that help will arrive promptly in the event of emergencies

correct_answers.text: I should know how I park and leave my vehicle if I am unable to continue driving
I should know how escape routes are indicated in tunnels

comment: If there is a tunnel on your route, you should know the appropriate traffic signs and behavioral measures in the event of a breakdown or an accident: in this case, alert the tunnel monitoring center and follow the next escape route. First, turn off the engine of your vehicle and leave the ignition key in the lock for rescue operations.

question_text:
While driving through a tunnel, you notice a fire in your vehicle. You are not able to exit the tunnel. What should you do?
I bring the vehicle to a halt as far to the right-side of the roadway as possible or park it in an emergency lay-by and

options.text: - turn on the hazard warning system
- switch off the engine
- leave the key in the ignition

correct_answers.text: - turn on the hazard warning system
- switch off the engine
- leave the key in the ignition

comment: If a fire in your vehicle prevents you from leaving a tunnel: Park the vehicle unlocked with the engine switched off and the ignition key remaining in the lock. Alarm the tunnel monitoring center. Take the next escape route on foot.

question_text: While driving in a tunnel you were forced to bring your vehicle to a halt due to a fire. What should you do now?

options.text: I trigger the fire alarm at the emergency call point
I extinguish the fire as best I can
I lock my vehicle

correct_answers.text: I trigger the fire alarm at the emergency call point
I extinguish the fire as best I can

comment: If you have to park your vehicle in a tunnel due to a fire, you should: stop the engine, leave the key in the ignition switch and quickly trigger the fire alarm at the emergency call station. Leave the tunnel as fast as possible on the next escape route.

question_text:
What should you anticipate?
That the truck in front of me

options.text: - will swing outwards even more
- will come to a sudden stop
- will remain stationary in the right-hand lane

correct_answers.text: - will swing outwards even more
- will come to a sudden stop

comment: You see that the truck wants to turn in front of you. The vehicle obscures the view of the traffic, so you need to adjust your speed. The truck probably swings out to take the curve. He might stop abruptly to let pedestrians or other road users pass.

question_text: What must you watch out for now?

options.text: For the vehicle on the road ahead
For the bicycle
For the motorbike

correct_answers.text: For the vehicle on the road ahead
For the bicycle

comment: You want to turn right, so does the car driver in front of you. The pedestrian traffic light of the cross street into which you want to turn shows green, and the pedestrian has priority. It is possible that your car in front will pull up and stop soon after to let the pedestrian pass. On the right you can also see a cyclist. The cyclist could drive past your vehicle on the right and circle your turning vehicle on the left. Avoid this danger.

question_text: Why are you required to stop here?

options.text: Because of the cyclist
Because of the green car
Because of the pedestrian

correct_answers.text: Because of the cyclist

comment: The cyclist must be given priority because she is on the right-of-way. Wait until the cyclist has passed the vehicles and driven through.

question_text: Why are you required to stop here?

options.text: Because of the red car
Because of the cyclist
Because of the pedestrian

correct_answers.text: Because of the red car

comment: The traffic on the main road is jammed. The red car drives around the parked vehicles to turn left. You have to wait and let this car pass as it has priority.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I keep a tight hold of the steering wheel and keep it pointed straight ahead
I swerve to the left
I swerve to the right

correct_answers.text: I keep a tight hold of the steering wheel and keep it pointed straight ahead

comment: When an animal walks on the road from the right, an evasive maneuver is a natural reflex. However, this can have far more fatal consequences than keeping the track. An evasive maneuver to the right may lead into the roadside ditch, one to the left may lead to a collision with oncoming traffic. It's safest to continue straight ahead.

question_text: What should you do now?

options.text: I perform an emergency braking manoeuvre
I sound my horn
I swerve to the left

correct_answers.text: I perform an emergency braking manoeuvre
I sound my horn

comment: You can see that the animal is about to run on the road. Horns may help stop it. In addition, you should initiate emergency braking to reduce a potential collision. Do not dodge! This rather leads to accidents with personal injury than a collision with an animal.

question_text: What must you look out for when the traffic lights turn green?

options.text: For [the pedestrian]
For the motorbike
For oncoming traffic

correct_answers.text: For [the pedestrian]
For the motorbike

comment: While you wait at the red light, a motorcyclist pushes past the waiting vehicles. When the traffic light switches to green you should pay attention to the motorcyclist and let him pass before he initiates a risky overtaking maneuver. But you should also let the pedestrian cross the road, which is still on the road despite it being green.

question_text: What must you be prepared for in this situation?

options.text: That oncoming traffic will appear
That the truck driver will jump down onto the carriageway
That traffic signs are concealed behind the truck

correct_answers.text: That oncoming traffic will appear
That the truck driver will jump down onto the carriageway
That traffic signs are concealed behind the truck

comment: The truck blocks your view. You can therefore recognize neither the oncoming traffic nor traffic signs behind the truck. Approach the vehicle at low speed. Look for oncoming traffic (they have priority) and keep your distance to the open driver's door when driving around. The driver of the truck could suddenly get out and jump onto the road.

question_text: What should you do when driving through a tunnel?

options.text: In a tunnel with oncoming traffic, I position myself towards the right-hand edge of the roadway
I memorise the safety features such as emergency exits and emergency telephones
I drive with a reduced distance to the vehicle ahead, so that I can use its tail lights as a guide
